content.thinking:
Let me analyze this certificate.

Certificate number: R60/2000-GB1-10.07
Scheme: A (OIML-CS certificates of conformity are typically scheme A... Actually this is an older R60 certificate. The scheme field asks for A|B. NWML certificates of conformity — these are typically scheme A certificates issued under the OIML Certificate System. I'll use "A".)

Project number: Ref: TS13/0002 — could be project_number. Hmm, "Ref: TS13/0002" appears in page 2. Could be reference number. I'll put project_number: "TS13/0002".

Page total: 3
Member state: United Kingdom
Date issued: 09 November 2010 → ISO format? The schema says date_issued. I'll use "2010-11-09".
OIML issuer id: not given explicitly. NWML is the issuer. The schema has oiml_issuer_id at certificate level; not present in markdown, so omit.

Issuing authority:
- name: National Weights and Measures Laboratory (Part of the National Measurement Office)
- address_lines: Stanton Avenue, Teddington, Middlesex, TW11 0JZ, United Kingdom
- person_responsible: Paul Dixon (or "Mr P R Dixon") — page 1 says "Paul Dixon- Product Certification Manager", page 2 says "Mr P R Dixon for NWML". person_title: Product Certification Manager
- oiml_issuer_id: omit

Applicants:
- B & T Weighing System (Kunshan) Co, Ltd, Zhu Jia Wan Road, Zhou Shi Town, Kunshan, Jiangsu, China

Manufacturers:
- "The applicant & T Scale Electronics Co., Ltd" — this means the manufacturer is the applicant AND T Scale Electronics Co., Ltd. So manufacturers: B & T Weighing System (Kunshan) Co., Ltd (same address as applicant) and T Scale Electronics Co., Ltd, No. 99, Shun-Chang Road, Kunshan, Jiangsu, China.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["TSNTI"]
- module_designation: "Analog load cell"? The description says "Stainless steel, shear beam strain gauge load cell". For R60 load cells, module designation would be "Analog load cell" — but the markdown doesn't say that explicitly. Hmm, rule says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. A strain gauge load cell is an analog load cell. But should I infer? The safest: since it's a strain gauge load cell, it's analog. I'll put "Analog load cell". Actually, don't fabricate — but strain gauge is analog by definition. I'll include it.
- description: "Stainless steel, shear beam strain gauge load cell"

Model family: The cert covers Emax values 500, 1000, 2000 kg. Also classification varies: C1, C2, C3, C3M, C4 with different nLC and Y values.

This is a two-dimensional matrix: accuracy class × Emax. The models could be defined by class variants. The page 1 table:
- Model designation: TSNTI
- Emax (kg): 500, 1000, 2000 (all models)
- Accuracy class: C
- n_max: 1000, 2000, 3000, 3000M, 4000 (5 columns corresponding to classes C1, C2, C3, C3M, C4)
- Vmin: Emax/5000, Emax/7000, Emax/12000, Emax/16000, Emax/16000
- pLC: 0.7

Page 3 Table 1 clarifies: Classification C1, C2, C3, C3M, C4 with nLC 1000, 2000, 3000, 3000, 4000 and Y values 5000, 7000, 12000, 16000, 16000. DR (Z) = 8000 for C3M only.

So the model variants are per accuracy class: TSNTI-C1, TSNTI-C2, TSNTI-C3, TSNTI-C3M, TSNTI-C4. Each available in Emax 500, 1000, 2000 kg.

How to structure? I think model_family with models per class:
- model_id: "TSNTI-C1" (label?), attributes... Or use class as model axis.

The characteristics.model_level could hold:
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc (nmax): values per class
- relative_vmin_y: values per class
- dr_ratio_z: values per class

But Emax is also multi-valued (500, 1000, 2000). Combined, models would be class × Emax = 15 combos. That might be overkill. The example in the schema for R60 shows models keyed by Emax value. Here the varying matrix dimension is primarily the accuracy class; Emax is a set of capacities available for the type.

I could emit model_family.models as class variants:
{"model_id": "TSNTI C1"}, {"model_id": "TSNTI C2"}, ... with attributes {accuracy_class: "C1", ...}.

And model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity_emax: values [{model: "TSNTI C1", value: {min:500, max:2000}?}] — no, it's a list of discrete values. Hmm. Lists of values are supposed to be a model matrix. But here Emax doesn't vary per class; it's common across all classes.

Alternative: models = class × Emax combos: "TSNTI C1 Emax=500kg", etc. 15 models. Then model_level attributes:
- maximum_capacity: 500 for C1 Emax=500, etc.
- nlc: 1000 for all C1 variants...

That's a full cross product. It's accurate but verbose. Given the guidance in the R60 example (models keyed by Emax), maybe the cleanest representation here:

model_family:
- family_name: "TSNTI"
- models: 15 entries? Or 5 class entries?

Let me think about what's most useful and faithful. The certificate covers one model designation TSNTI with variants classified C1–C4, each in capacities 500/1000/2000 kg. I'll do models keyed by class, with Emax as a matrix table, plus matrix_tables preserving the original tables.

Actually the schema example for R60 with "25,30,50,60,75,90" makes models "Emax=25t" etc. Here we have two varying dimensions. I think the best approach:

model_family.models: 5 entries per class:
- {"model_id": "TSNTI-C1", "label": "Class C1", "attributes": {"accuracy_class": "C1"}}
- etc.

characteristics.model_level: attributes varying by class:
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: C1→1000, C2→2000, C3→3000, C3M→3000, C4→4000
- relative_vmin_y_emax_over_vmin: C1→5000, C2→7000, C3→12000, C3M→16000, C4→16000
- dr_ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: C1→null, C2→null, C3→null, C3M→8000, C4→null (only for C3M; note in page 1 table it's 3000M → Emax/16000; page 3 the Z=8000 only for C3M)

For Emax, since it's common: type_level: maximum_capacity with value {min:500, max:2000}? No — it's a discrete set {500, 1000, 2000}, not a range. Hmm. The value shape allows number | {min,max} | string. A discrete set isn't a range. I could keep it as string "500, 1000, 2000"? That violates "numbers, not strings" a bit, but the value rules say lists of values should be a model matrix. Since Emax is constant across classes, the model matrix dimension is class. Maybe I should make models class×Emax after all.

Let me reconsider: make models = 15 variants with model_id like "TSNTI-C1-500kg". Then:

model_level:
- maximum_capacity_emax: 15 values (500/1000/2000 per model)
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 15 values (1000 ×3, 2000 ×3, 3000 ×3, 3000 ×3, 4000 ×3)
- relative_vmin (as Y ratio or Vmin formula): 15 values ("Emax/5000" etc. or 5000 etc.)
- dr_ratio_z: only C3M variants → 8000; others null/omit.

This is faithful and complete. 15 models × 3 attributes. It's verbose but correct. Alternatively keep it simpler with class-keyed models and represent Emax as a type-level discrete set stored in matrix_tables.

I think I'll go with 15 models for full cross-product fidelity, and also include matrix_tables preserving both the page-1 table and Table 1 (Essential technical data). Actually matrix_tables for Table 1 would duplicate model_level. The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The class table fits model_level reasonably. But the Table 1 has more: rated output, excitation voltage, impedance, temperature, safe overload, cable length — all constant (type-level).

Decision:
- model_family.family_name: "TSNTI"
- models: 15 entries (class × Emax).
- characteristics.model_level: nlc, y (relative vmin), z (only C3M), emax (per model).
- type_level: minimum dead load relative (0.5 %), rated output (2 ± 0.2 mV/V — value {min:1.8, max:2.2}? Actually "2 ± 0.2 %" — hmm the units cell says mV/V, and the value includes "± 0.2 %". So rated output is 2 mV/V with tolerance ±0.2%? Or 2 ± 0.2 mV/V? The table shows "2 ± 0.2 %" then Units mV/V. Likely rated output 2 mV/V ±0.2% (relative tolerance). I'll record rated_output: value 2, unit mV/V, and maybe rated_output_tolerance: 0.2 %. To be safe: value: "2 ± 0.2 %"? Rule: structured strict — numbers not strings. I'll split: rated_output {value: 2, unit_symbol: "mV/V"}, rated_output_tolerance {value: 0.2, unit_symbol: "%"}. Hmm, but it could be ±0.2 mV/V. The "%" suggests relative. I'll note value 0.2 unit "%".
- maximum excitation voltage: 18, V AC, DC → unit_symbol "V"; maybe power type AC/DC. I'll set unit_symbol "V" and add maximum_excitation_voltage_type "AC, DC"? Simpler: value 18, unit_symbol "V", and separate characteristic excitation_voltage_type: "AC, DC". Might be overkill; I'll include it.
- input impedance rlc: 350 ± 5 Ω → value {min: 345, max: 355}, unit Ω.
- temperature rating: -10/+40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C. Note: -10/+40 could be -10 to +40.
- safe overload relative elim/emax: 150 % → value 150, unit "%".
- cable length: 5 m.
- additional characteristics: "4 wire (0.25 mm²)" and note "Class C3M is suitable for multi interval instruments." → description strings.
- apportionment factor pLC: 0.7 (dimensionless).
- accuracy class: "C" per page 1, but Table 1 shows C1–C4. Recommendation accuracy_classes: ["C1","C2","C3","C3M","C4"].

Footnotes: none present.

Test reports:
- Centro SIT n° 44, Test Report No P98107_500_C4, 23 pages, role: test_report
- Centro SIT n° 44, Test Report No P98062_1000_C3M, 23 pages, role: test_report

The id field: "P98107_500_C4" and "P98062_1000_C3M". Dates not given.

Revision history:
- revision: "10.07"? The issue no is R60/2000-GB1-10.07. The certificate history table: ISSUE NO R60/2000-GB1-10.07, DATE 09 November 2010, DESCRIPTION "Type approval first issued." Revision: "10.07"? The schema example: revision (string e.g. "0"). I'll use "10.07" — that seems to be the issue suffix. Hmm, or the revision could be "GB1-10.07". The certificate number format R60/2000-GB1-10.07: GB1 = UK certificate 1, 10.07 = year 2010, revision 07? NWML certs typically R60/2000-GBn-YY.NN where NN is revision number. I'll put revision: "10.07" to be safe as it's the distinguishing suffix. Actually maybe just "10.07" is fine with date and changes.

Recommendation:
- id: "R60", edition: 2000, amendment: null, scheme: "A", accuracy_classes: ["C1","C2","C3","C3M","C4"]. Page 1 says accuracy class C, page 2 says "accuracy class: C". Table 1 shows C1–C4. Hmm — page 1/2 say class C; Table 1 lists C1, C2, C3, C3M, C4. So accuracy classes covered are C1, C2, C3, C3M, C4. I'll use those.

Scheme: The OIML Certificate System (pre-2013 basic system) — certificates like this are under the "OIML Certificate System for measuring instruments" which corresponds to scheme A in the OIML-CS. I'll say "A".

Now models: 15 entries. model_id: "TSNTI-C1-500kg"? Let me construct: family TSNTI; models:
- TSNTI C1 Emax=500kg
- TSNTI C1 Emax=1000kg
- TSNTI C1 Emax=2000kg
- ... C2, C3, C3M, C4 similarly.

Attributes per model: accuracy_class, maximum_capacity_kg.

model_level entries:
1. attribute: "maximum_capacity", unit_symbol: "kg", values: 15 entries {model, value}.
2. attribute: "max_load_cell_intervals_nlc", unit_symbol: null, values: 15 entries.
3. attribute: "relative_vmin_y_emax_over_vmin", unit_symbol: null, values: 15 entries (5000, 7000, 12000, 16000, 16000 repeated ×3 each).
4. attribute: "dr_ratio_z_emax_over_2dr", unit_symbol: null, values: only C3M models have 8000; others null. Include all 15 with null for non-C3M? Or omit null values? I'll include only C3M entries with value 8000 — values array can just list the C3M models. Hmm, but the schema shows values per model. I'll include entries with value null for the others to be explicit. Actually cleaner: include all 15, null where "-".

Also Vmin (kg): page 1 gives Vmin as formulas Emax/5000 etc. I have Y = Emax/Vmin ratio which captures it. The canonical label from rule 1: "Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval(1) Y=Emax/vmin" → "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin". So use "relative_vmin_y_emax_over_vmin" or "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin". I'll use "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin".

For Z: "Relative DR (ratio to minimum dead load output return) Z = Emax/(2*DR)" → "dr_ratio_z_emax_over_2dr" or "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr". I'll use "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr".

n_max: "Maximum number of load cell intervals, n_max" (page 1) vs page 3 "Maximum number of load cell verification intervals n_LC" → canonical "max_load_cell_intervals_nlc". Use that.

Emax: "maximum_capacity" (rule 1 example: Maximum capacity ($E_{max}$) → maximum_capacity).

Type-level:
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7
- minimum_dead_load_relative: 0.5 % (Emin/Emax). Label "minimum_dead_load_relative_emin_over_emax"? Value 0.5, unit "%".
- rated_output: 2 mV/V; rated_output_tolerance: 0.2 %
- maximum_excitation_voltage: 18 V (AC, DC)
- input_impedance_rlc: {min:345, max:355} Ω
- temperature_rating: {min:-10, max:40} °C
- safe_load_limit_relative / safe overload relative elim/emax: 150 % → label "safe_overload_relative_elim_over_emax"? Rule example: "150% of Emax" → safe_overload 150 % + safe_overload_reference "Emax". I'll use "safe_overload_relative": value 150, unit "%". Or "safe_load_limit_relative". I'll go "safe_overload_relative".
- cable_length: 5 m
- additional_characteristics: value "4 wire (0.25 mm²)" — as string value. And class C3M note: "Class C3M is suitable for multi interval instruments." I could add to description or as note. I'll add "c3m_note" or include in description. I'll put in description field of certified_type? The description currently is "Stainless steel, shear beam strain gauge load cell". I'll append the multi-interval note maybe as a footnote-ish. I'll add type_level characteristic "multi_interval_suitability" only for C3M... Actually simpler: keep additional_characteristics: "4 wire (0.25 mm²)" and add "notes": not in schema. I'll put "Class C3M is suitable for multi interval instruments." into matrix_tables description or footnotes. Footnotes are for footnote markers. I'll add it as part of the Table 1 matrix table description? The matrix table entry could capture Table 1 wholesale. Let me include one matrix_table for "Essential technical data" preserving everything, with footnotes [] and description noting C3M multi-interval suitability. That preserves fidelity.

Actually, should I include matrix_tables at all given model_level captures the varying part? The Table 1 includes additional marking "-", additional characteristics. I'll include matrix_tables with name "Essential technical data (Table 1)" capturing rows. That's helpful.

matrix_tables entry:

}

rows: [
  {"characteristic": "maximum_load_cell_verification_intervals", "symbol": "nLC", "C1": 1000, "C2": 2000, "C3": 3000, "C3M": 3000, "C4": 4000, "units": null},
  {"characteristic": "maximum_capacity", "symbol": "Emax", "C1": "500, 1000, 2000", ...} — messy with values.

That's a good pivot representation. And then model_level per model (class × Emax). This may duplicate but it's fine.

Hmm, wait. Maybe I'm overcomplicating with 15 models. Let me reconsider whether models should be class-based only, with Emax as type-level discrete set. The R60 example in rules: "25,30,50,60,75,90" → 6 models "Emax=25t" etc. Here the equivalent comma-list is Emax "500, 1000, 2000" → 3 capacity variants. But there's also the class dimension. Combining both: 15.

I'll go with 15 models: model_id "TSNTI-C1-500" etc. with label like "Class C1, Emax 500 kg". attributes: {"accuracy_class": "C1", "maximum_capacity_kg": 500}.

- apportionment_factor_plc: {value: 0.7, unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null}
- minimum_dead_load_relative: {value: 0.5, unit_symbol: "%"} — note Emin/Emax = 0.5%. Label: "minimum_dead_load_relative_emin_over_emax".

Characteristics value objects: schema in rules shows {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. footnote_markers optional (empty/omit). I'll include unit_id: null always? The rule says leave unit_id null unless certain. Including "unit_id": null is fine.

Should type_level values include footnote_markers? Not needed; omit.

Also accuracy class "C" from page 1 — represented in models/attributes and recommendation.accuracy_classes.

matrix_tables: include the pivoted class table as described. Also maybe include page-1 table? The page-1 table is essentially the same info (nmax and Vmin per class). One matrix table suffices; description can note Vmin formulas.

Let me also double check "Rated output: 2 ± 0.2 %" with Units "mV/V". Interpreted: rated output 2 mV/V, tolerance ±0.2% (relative). I'll record rated_output 2 mV/V and rated_output_tolerance 0.2 %.

Ref TS13/0002 as project_number — it's an internal reference of NWML. Include.

Final JSON assembly. Keep it parseable, no comments.

One more consideration: "characteristics.model_level[]" entries shape: {attribute, unit, values[]} — schema says unit; rules examples use "unit_symbol". The example JSON uses "unit_symbol". I'll use "unit_symbol" consistently (and "unit_id": null too? example shows only unit_symbol in model_level; I'll add unit_id: null for consistency with structured values rule... The model_level example: {"attribute": "qmax", "unit_symbol": "m³/h", "values": [...]}. values contain {model, value} without unit objects. I'll follow that: values items {model, value, footnote_markers?}. For structured strictness at type_level I'll use full objects {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}.

Write it out.
